newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran president-elect calls for easing tensions.
newsitem.headline: Iran president-elect calls for easing tensions.

text.p: Moderate president-elect Mohammad Khatami on Thursday called for tensions to be eased in Iran's foreign relations, but said all factions should unite against threats from the country's enemies.

"We have always been for an honorable peace coupled with dignity and independence of the country and to this end the Islamic Iran has followed and will always pursue a policy of easing tension in its relations with other countries," Khatami said in remarks quoted by the Iranian news agency IRNA.

"Referring to the hostility and threats of enemies, the president-elect called for a united front to ward off these threats adding that all forces from every wing and faction should work in unity to repel these threats," the news agency said.
Khatami, a Shi'ite Moslem cleric who was elected by a landslide last month, repeatedly called during his campaign for world conflicts to be resolved through dialogue.
But analysts said he was not expected to make radical changes in foreign policy, the domain of Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

The election of Khatami, who defeated a candidate backed by Iran's conservative clerical establishment, is seen by some U.S. analysts as likely to increase the pressure on President Bill Clinton from European allies to rethink the long U.S. drive to isolate Iran as a "rogue nation".

Germany and other European countries including France are expected to use the poll results asgrounds to patch up ties with Iran, downgraded after a German court concluded in April that Iranian leaders had ordered the 1992 killing of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin. Iran has repeatedly denied the charges.
Before the verdict, Germany had been the main champion of the European Union's policy of "critical dialogue" with Iran, despite the United States' policy of isolating the country.

Khatami was speaking at the mausoleum of revolutionary leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini to mark the day in 1963 when thousands of demonstrators confronted police to protest against Khomeini's arrest after he made a fiery speech denouncing Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi.
The day, known as the 15th of Khordad Uprising after its date in the Iranian calendar, was the first mass action inspired by Khomeini and foreshadowed the 1979 Islamic revolution. FS
